text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Anglican church in Kenya, opposition leaders and fiery Moslem leader Sheikh Khalid Balala jointly condemn President Daniel arap Moi, saying his days as leader are numbered if he continues to reject dialogue.
- Sheikh Balala calls for comprehensive constitutional reforms.
- President Moi's son Jonathan Toroitich defends the head of state against accusations of misrule.
- Cabinet Minister Nicholas Biwott says the ruling Kenya African National Union party is ready for political reforms and dialogue with those who value peace and stability.
- A mother, who is apparently mentally disturbed and from Bomet district in the Rift Valley, is suspected of cooking and eating her three-month old baby.
- Former political detainee Koigi wa Wamwere welcomes President Moi's pledge to call the ruling party's top organs to discuss constitutional reforms.

- Sheikh Khalid Balala's campaign to restore the dignity and prosperity of Kenyans on his return home starts off on a sore note when a group of Moslems accuse him of desecrating their house of worship.
- Vice President George Saitoti warns of political uncertainty if the country gives in to sectarian pressure for hasty constitutional reforms.
- Rift Valley politicians start talks to ease political tension building in the country after violent calls for constitutional reforms.
